newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais climbs on bullish outlook.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais climbs on bullish outlook.

text.p: Shares in state-controlled Credit Lyonnais were up by nearly eight percent on Thursday on the back of a bullish 1997 profit outlook by the French bank.
At 1042 GMT, the shares were trading 7.63 percent or 14.5 francs higher at 204.50 francs after at least one investment house raised its recommendation on the shares.

The bank, which has been digging out from an expansion binge that plunged it deeply into the red, reported late Thursday a slim 1996 profit rise to 202 million francs from a profit of 13 million in 1995 but a sharply improved underlying performance and forecast net profits in the billions of francs for 1997.

Paris brokerage Transbourse switched its recommendation to "buy" from "sell", citing the bank's good control of general expenses, stabilisation of net banking income and strong growth in gross operating profit.
"One has the feeling that Credit Lyonnais can rebound," said analyst Patrick Leguil of Transbourse.
He said that the bank still faced challenges in such areas as improving its efficiency ratio but that it was closing the gap on its rivals.
